resources.string: Known trackers, malware and phishing sites are being blocked on this phone.
Turn on the switch to start filtering.
If Settings → Network → Private DNS is set to a provider hostname, Android skips this filter. Set it to Off or Automatic.

PrivacyGuard uses a local VPN on this phone to check website lookups (DNS). Lookups for known trackers, malware and phishing sites are blocked; all others go to your normal DNS server.\n\nNo VPN server is used. Nothing is sent to us, and no data leaves your phone because of this app.

Blocks adult sites. Their names are never shown in the app.
Blocks public encrypted DNS, VPN and proxy services that apps and browsers could use to get around the filter.
Blocks machine-generated domains registered in the past week, often used for malware. Large list; can block a new legitimate site now and then.
Blocks sites that use your phone to mine cryptocurrency.
Blocks the servers of known stalkerware apps that secretly report on a phone.
Unlock Pro on the Pro tab to use this.
If your network\'s DNS server doesn\'t answer, ask Cloudflare (1.1.1.1) or Google (8.8.8.8) instead. Off by default, because those lookups then leave the phone to that company.

PrivacyGuard filters website lookups on your phone. It collects no personal data, has no account and no server. Blocked lookups never leave the phone; other lookups go to your network\'s normal DNS server (and, only if you turn on Public DNS fallback, to Cloudflare or Google when that server doesn\'t answer).

Asks for a PIN before protection can be turned off or filters changed. It can\'t stop someone from turning off the VPN in Android\'s settings or uninstalling the app; for that, use Android\'s Always-on VPN and parental controls.
Forgot the PIN? Clear the app\'s storage in Android settings. Pro comes back from Google Play; your filters and rules must be set again.
